userStories.title: Finish the shootout fix: series_sim and shutout pivots derive winners from the win column (R3-M1)
userStories.description: As the tool owner, I want the two remaining copies of the condemned tied-goal pivot fixed so the game-win model is served the same feature universe it is trained on. (CODE_REVIEW_R3 R3-M1) Evidence: US-203 fixed only game_win.py; series_sim.py:330 (_pivot_all_games) and shutout.py:291 (_pivot_games) still filter games.loc[home_goals != away_goals], and series_sim derives home_won by goal comparison at line 491 — so reconstruct_series_matchups (the production pre-series snapshot path feeding projection artifacts and both backtests) excludes all 1,024 shootout games (7.1% of 14,508 decided games) from Elo/win_pct/points state while the retrained model includes them. Measured serve-vs-train skew at the 2026 R1 freeze: VGK Elo +35.8, PIT +19.4, EDM +17.1, win_pct up to 5.1pp. shutout.py additionally drops 16 genuine 0-0 shootout wins from its training universe.
acceptanceCriteria: Read ml/SPEC.md AND the R3-M1 finding in ml/CODE_REVIEW_R3.md in full before starting

series_sim._pivot_all_games and shutout._pivot_games derive the winner from the archive 'win' column (same pattern as game_win.py post-US-203); series_sim.py:491's home_won comes from the win column too; genuinely undecided rows still excluded loudly

Real-archive count tests for BOTH modules: pivot row count equals unique decided games (14,508 total across the 11 archives; shutout's pre-fix 13,484 is the regression number); a real SO game asserts the correct winner in each module
The 16 genuine 0-0 shootout wins enter build_shutout_dataset as shutout wins for the SO winner (NHL stats rules) — asserted on at least one real example

Train/serve consistency check: for one real season, the pre-series snapshot Elo from reconstruct_series_matchups matches the training-path Elo trajectory for the same team/date (the R3-M1 divergence measurement goes to ~0) — asserted with a tolerance, and series_sim's 'exact same update rules' docstring is true again

HONESTY GATE: series-sim/shutout/game-win metrics will move; report the honest numbers in progress.txt — never tune seeds/splits/baselines to preserve old values. Committed evidence regeneration is deferred to US-305

userStories.title: Draft-night input safety: session clobber, duplicate managers, strict --eliminated, honest recommend label (R3-m9, R3-m10, R3-m11, R3-m8)
userStories.description: As the tool owner, I want the CLI to protect me from my own draft-night typos, because round 3 demonstrated live: (R3-m9) launching 'oracle draft' autosaves BEFORE the input loop (cli/draft.py:664) so a quit-only session silently wipes an existing ./draft-session.json to 0 picks — and I draft in TWO 2026 leagues on the same nights, making the collision the default; (R3-m10) '--managers ben,ben,kyle,levi' passes validation, giving 'oracle recommend' a misleading deep ValueError and 'oracle draft' a silently merged two-seat roster; (R3-m11) '--eliminated MON' (Montreal is MTL) silently drops the unmatched token, leaving the team draftable; (R3-m8) standalone 'oracle recommend' still prints plain 'fitted opponents' when seatN/case-typo names zero the affinity signal — the interactive path already has the honest three-state label.
acceptanceCriteria: Read ml/SPEC.md AND the R3-m8..m11 findings in ml/CODE_REVIEW_R3.md in full before starting

Session clobber: starting a session never silently overwrites an existing session file — refuse with a clear message (offer --resume or a different --session path) or uniquify the default filename; the round-3 quit-only reproduction (2-pick log -> 0 picks) is the regression test
Duplicate manager ids are rejected at parse time with a clear message in BOTH 'oracle draft' and 'oracle recommend' (and DraftState.new validates uniqueness as defense in depth); tested
--eliminated raises a clear error naming any token that matches no team in the pool (valid case-insensitive abbrevs keep working); tested with the MON/XYZ cases

'oracle recommend' (cli/project.py:641) reuses the interactive path's three-state opponent label (plain fitted / mixed / league-average-no-affinity) or emits an equivalent warning; the default seat1..seat4 invocation must not print plain 'fitted opponents'; tested — also cover the case-typo real-name case ('Ben' vs 'ben')

userStories.title: Guard hygiene: fresh-clone skips, provenance ancestry, call-site isolation guard, goalie ownership (R3-m2, R3-m4, R3-m5, R3-m1)
userStories.description: As the tool owner, I want the guards themselves airtight: (R3-m2) test_real_2026_league_comparisons_never_pool_leagues (tests/test_backtest.py:858) and test_real_2024_levi_r3_4_roster_scores_corrected_64_points (:906) read gitignored data/normalized/*.parquet with no existence check — on a fresh clone the suite is 2 failed / 690 passed, and README's 'Run tests' documents no generation prerequisite; (R3-m4) the provenance test accepts any 40-hex git_sha, so a stale artifact from any old commit passes (today's split tree — models at da5e568, fixtures at 8000f5b — is the demonstration); (R3-m5) hardcoding the grouping inside _build_choices (opponents.py:385) re-merges the 2026 cross-league pools and changes fitted coefficients yet passes all 695 tests, because the isolation tests call _event_keys themselves (same wiring at _membership_for_season:899 and _per_pick_accuracy:954); (R3-m1) _mark_duplicate_ownership excludes goalie/team slots, so two managers owning the same team's goalie slot would pass silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Read ml/SPEC.md AND the R3-m1/m2/m4/m5 findings in ml/CODE_REVIEW_R3.md in full before starting

The two real-data regression tests use the same pytest.skip pattern as their siblings (test_opponents.py:498, test_entity_match.py:519) when data/normalized files are absent; verified: the full suite passes (with skips) in a clean worktree with no generated data; README's test section documents the three-command generation prerequisite (normalize, league-drafts + match-drafts, odds) for running the real-data tests

test_committed_model_evidence asserts each manifest git_sha is an ancestor of HEAD (subprocess git merge-base --is-ancestor, skipping gracefully outside a git checkout) AND that all manifests regenerated by one evidence pass share one sha (the 2026-r* fixtures may carry their own single shared sha; encode the expected relationship, not just format)

The league-isolation guard goes through the production call path: either a coefficient-level assertion on the real-parquet fit or a test that patches/inspects _build_choices grouping — verified by re-applying the round-3 surviving mutant (hardcode ['season','draft_event','base_position'] inside _build_choices) and confirming a named test now fails
